main_diagnosis: The M-current time constant function `tau_w_fn` returns values on the order of 0.06–0.15 ms — roughly three orders of magnitude too fast for physiological M/KCNQ kinetics (~50–200 ms). At rest (V ≈ −65 mV, V_half_M ≈ −35 mV) the denominator `Exp(-30/40)+Exp(30/20) ≈ 4.95`, giving tau_w ≈ 1/(3.3×4.95) ≈ 0.061 ms. With such a tiny time constant the gate `w` collapses to its steady state `w_inf` within a single integration step, so the M-current provides no slow adaptation whatsoever and is effectively indistinguishable from a static conductance. This makes the added channel unable to reshape inter-spike intervals, mean stimulation voltage, or voltage distribution statistics, explaining the poor NLE score.

issues.description: tau_w_fn produces time constants ~0.06–0.15 ms because the numerator is 1.0. Physiological M-current (KCNQ/Kv7) has time constants of ~20–200 ms. The missing scaling factor makes the gate quasi-instantaneous, destroying the slow-adaptation purpose of the channel and degrading all summary statistics that depend on inter-spike dynamics.
issues.suggestion: Replace the numerator 1.0 with a value in the range 100–300 (milliseconds scale), e.g. `return 200.0 / (3.3 * denom + 1e-7)`. This shifts tau_w to ~20–100 ms at typical sub-threshold voltages, giving the gate the slow time course needed for genuine spike-frequency adaptation and improved matching of the voltage-distribution and spike-count summary statistics.

issues.description: nois_fact_obs is hard-coded to 0.0, completely suppressing observation noise on the returned voltage trace. Because the target recordings include measurement/channel noise, statistics such as resting-potential standard deviation, voltage variance, skewness, and kurtosis cannot be matched regardless of how well the deterministic dynamics are tuned.
issues.suggestion: Either (a) tie observation noise to the already-inferred `nois_fact` parameter (e.g. `nois_fact_obs = nois_fact * scale` with a small fixed scale ≈ 0.1–0.5), or (b) use a small fixed non-zero value such as `nois_fact_obs = 0.5`. This will allow the model to reproduce the empirical variance and higher-order moments of the resting and stimulation-period voltage distributions.
